scenarios.question: When an MCP tool handler raises MCPError, which channel carries the failure back to the client?
scenarios.hypothesis_title: protocol errors collapse into tool-result errors
scenarios.probe_action: Route the request through the v2 error path and verify that the failure is delivered as JSON-RPC error.
scenarios.recommendation: Keep protocol-level MCPError on the JSON-RPC error channel instead of converting it into CallToolResult(isError=true).

scenarios.question: Does the client receive the structured JSON-RPC error code from an MCP tool handler that raises MCPError?
scenarios.hypothesis_title: structured protocol error codes are discarded
scenarios.probe_action: Use the v2 error path and verify that code -32000 survives the client/server boundary.
scenarios.recommendation: Preserve the original MCPError code across the transport so callers can make retry and escalation decisions without parsing text.

scenarios.question: Does the client retain MCPError data when a tool call raises a protocol-level failure?
scenarios.hypothesis_title: structured error data is lost in v1
scenarios.probe_action: Use the v2 error path and verify that the structured data payload survives the client/server boundary.
scenarios.recommendation: Preserve structured MCPError data so agent runtimes can distinguish protocol failures from ordinary tool execution failures.

scenarios.question: Does a normal MCP tool call still return its successful result?
Does a normal Python exception inside an MCP tool remain a tool execution error?
Does the MCP client still discover the probe tool through tools/list?
